text:
Welcome to Issue 87 of the weekly developer tooling roundup.

Each week we sort through new releases, updates, and side projects so you can spend less time searching and more time building. This week there are five links, and three of them are worth a closer look.

First, a new Rust linter. If you've wanted stricter checks than your current setup gives you, or clearer explanations when something gets flagged, this one is worth a look. It aims to catch subtle mistakes early without burying you in noise.

Next, a Git GUI. Some of us live in the terminal, but there are times when seeing branches, diffs, and history laid out visually saves real time. This one focuses on speed and a clean layout.

Finally, a tracing tool for anyone who has tried to figure out where the time goes in a request. It helps you follow execution across your system and find bottlenecks without guessing.

The other two links fill out the issue with smaller finds we think you'll enjoy.

Thanks for reading, and welcome to the newest of our 9,400 subscribers. Let's dig in.
